criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use a fixed oblique isometric projection with paired diagonal ground axes.
Buildings and pylons share a consistent elevated map viewpoint.
different: REFERENCE frames larger focal infrastructure, while CANDIDATE exposes broader, flatter tile fields.
CANDIDATE has a slightly shallower pitch and more explicit terrain tiling.

evidence.observation: G02 shows an elevated isometric view with two clear diagonal world axes.
G02 preserves the isometric axes but reveals a flatter, more visibly tiled ground plane.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Pylons are taller than nearby low buildings in both images.
Smokestacks and utility structures serve as mid-size landmarks in both.
different: REFERENCE plants and substations form dominant compound silhouettes; CANDIDATE facilities are smaller and fragmented among repeated buildings.
CANDIDATE pylons read oversized against houses, while REFERENCE tower-to-plant proportions are more balanced.

evidence.observation: G01 is dominated by a large integrated plant, with the adjacent pylon subordinate to the compound.
G01 contains small repeated buildings beside a comparatively large pylon and smokestack.
G08 presents a large industrial complex as the primary mass.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use charcoal soil and metal, muted concrete, and sparse amber illumination.
Cyan network accents contrast strongly against dark warm midtones in both.
different: REFERENCE has painterly blackened metal, atmospheric depth, and dense surface variation.
CANDIDATE reads as flatter tiled terrain with brown sprite edges and weaker material cohesion.

evidence.observation: G08 shows layered soot, metal, smoke, warm windows, and varied industrial surfaces.
G08 uses flatter repeated tiles and building sprites with limited atmospheric depth.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both distinguish cyan energized routes from amber planned routes.
Both combine routes with lattice pylons and circular or lettered network markers.
different: REFERENCE conductors converge on towers and form cohesive corridors; CANDIDATE routes frequently pass or float beside towers without clear attachment.
CANDIDATE mixes solid strands, dashed paths, node links, and selection geometry with a less consistent hierarchy.

evidence.observation: G04 clearly separates a cyan energized corridor from an amber dotted tower route.
G01 has cyan parallel strands and an amber dashed path, but the nearby pylons are not visibly attached.
G06 uses amber node links, lettered markers, route dashes, and several towers with competing visual hierarchy.
